messages.content:
A regular hexagon with side length 4 is subdivided into a lattice of 96 equilateral triangles of side length 1. Let $S$ be the set of all vertices of this lattice. Compute the number of nondegenerate triangles with vertices in $S$ that contain the center of the hexagon strictly in their interior.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(O\) be the center of the hexagon. Since a triangle containing \(O\) strictly in its interior cannot have \(O\) as a vertex, we only need to consider the \(60\) nonzero lattice vertices.

Use triangular-lattice coordinates generated by two unit vectors at \(60^\circ\). A lattice point is represented by \((a,b)\in\mathbb Z^2\), and the side-\(4\) hexagon centered at the origin is

\[
|a|\le 4,\qquad |b|\le 4,\qquad |a+b|\le 4.
\]

For a line through the origin, take a primitive direction \((a,b)\) up to sign. Define

\[
M=\max(|a|,|b|,|a+b|).
\]

The number of lattice points on either ray of that line inside the hexagon is

\[
m=\left\lfloor \frac{4}{M}\right\rfloor.
\]

Enumerating the unoriented primitive lines gives:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
M & m=\lfloor 4/M\rfloor & \text{number of lines} & \text{representatives }(a,b)\\ \hline
1 & 4 & 3 & (1,0),(0,1),(1,-1)\\
2 & 2 & 3 & (1,1),(1,-2),(2,-1)\\
3 & 1 & 6 & (1,2),(1,-3),(2,1),(2,-3),(3,-1),(3,-2)\\
4 & 1 & 6 & (1,3),(1,-4),(3,1),(3,-4),(4,-1),(4,-3)
\end{array}
\]

So the line-weight multiset is

\[
4,4,4,\; 2,2,2,\; \underbrace{1,\dots,1}_{12\text{ times}}.
\]

For three nonzero points, the origin is strictly inside their triangle iff their direction angles are not contained in any closed semicircle, equivalently the largest angular gap between the three rays is strictly less than \(\pi\). For any three distinct lines through the origin, exactly two of the \(2^3\) choices of one ray from each line satisfy this condition. Therefore, if the three chosen line weights are \(m_i,m_j,m_k\), their contribution is

\[
2m_i m_j m_k.
\]

Hence the desired number is

\[
2\sum_{i<j<k} m_i m_j m_k.
\]

The sum \(\sum m_i m_j m_k\) is the coefficient of \(x^3\) in

\[
(1+4x)^3(1+2x)^3(1+x)^{12}.
\]

Now

\[
(1+4x)^3(1+2x)^3
=1+18x+132x^2+504x^3+O(x^4),
\]

and

\[
(1+x)^{12}=1+12x+66x^2+220x^3+\cdots.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{i<j<k} m_i m_j m_k
=504+132\cdot 12+18\cdot 66+220
=3496.
\]

Therefore the total number of nondegenerate triangles containing the center strictly in their interior is

\[
2\cdot 3496 = 6992.
\]

\[
\boxed{6992}
\]
